Backed mode

Source: R/backed.R
anndata-backed.Rd

Internal pieces of backed mode (file_backing.py, read_h5ad_backed). read_h5ad(backed = ) keeps X and raw$X on disk while every other Slot is read into memory, and the backing file is held by an AnnDataFileManager (adata$file).

Arguments

filename

Path of the backing file.

filemode

"r" or "r+".

key

Name of a member of the file, such as "X" or "raw/X".

value

A value to write.

manager

An AnnDataFileManager.

path

Path of the array within the file.

shape

The shape of the array, rows then columns.

encoding

The Encoding type, "array", "csr_matrix" or "csc_matrix".

dtype

The dtype of the stored values.

store

An open rhdf5 file handle.

call

The call reported by errors.

Details

The manager remembers the file name and mode, and opens read-only for "r" and read-write for "r+". close() closes the handle but keeps the file name, so the object stays backed, and reading X (or raw$X) opens the file again. A finalizer closes the handle when the manager is garbage collected. Unlike Python only the modes "r" and "r+" open, because "w" would truncate the backing file.

A backed_x stands for X or raw$X on disk. It records where the array is and finds the open file through the manager, so it survives a close. A dense array is also a backed_dense (R/backed-dense.R) and a sparse matrix a backed_sparse (R/backed-sparse.R).
